arguments.message:
Hi there! Meridian webhooks never silently truncate a payload – when a record’s full content would exceed the fixed payload size the webhook sends only an `id` with `truncated: true`. Your consumer should treat that flag as a signal to fetch the complete record via the API.

Also, the number of webhook calls can’t be reduced on our side – each change is delivered as its own event. Any “batching” has to be done on the receiving side: buffer the incoming events, then fetch the full records (or the ones flagged as truncated) in batches from the API and process them together.

So the strategy is:
1. Listen to each webhook event as it arrives.
2. When you see `truncated: true`, call the API to retrieve the full record.
3. Accumulate those fetched records in your own queue or batch processor and handle them in groups of your choosing.

This way you stay within the payload limit and still get the benefits of batch processing on your end.
